destination.name: Byron Bay
destination.tagline: A surf town beside Cape Byron, with beaches, a lighthouse and hinterland villages.
destination.description: Byron Bay is a coastal town in the far north-east of New South Wales, about 800 km north of Sydney and 175 km south of Brisbane. Cape Byron, beside it, is the easternmost point of mainland Australia, and Captain Cook named it in 1770. Visitors come for the surf at Main Beach, The Pass and Wategos, diving and snorkelling at Julian Rocks, and the hinterland villages of Bangalow and Mullumbimby. Temperate and tropical waters meet offshore.
whyVisit: Surf or swim at Wategos Beach
See giant geodes at Crystal Castle

goodToKnow.title: Lighthouse parking
goodToKnow.detail: Parking at the lighthouse costs $10 (Wikivoyage); the walk from the start of the track along the beach takes about 20 minutes.

goodToKnow.title: Getting in and out
goodToKnow.detail: Ewingsdale Road from the motorway is slow in summer and school holidays; Wikivoyage suggests leaving at the Lennox Head exit (Ross Lane) and entering from the south.

goodToKnow.title: Where to swim
goodToKnow.detail: Main Beach is patrolled all summer and others at Christmas school holidays; Wikivoyage says winter daytime temperatures average around 20 C.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Come in {months}: they fall between winter, when days average about 20 C, and the summer and school-holiday traffic on Ewingsdale Road.
